evidence_reviewed: witness_monitor_output: validation-enrichment and aml-compliance DOWN at 07:23:53.7 / 07:23:55.4, both RECOVERED shortly after
ES query clearflow-*,clearflow-healthmonitor-* range 07:23:47 to 07:25:07: validation-enrichment/aml-compliance repeated MongoHealthIndicator ~30000ms timeout WARN events in lockstep
validation-enrichment ERROR events: "Timed out while waiting for a server that matches WritableServerSelector" on real paymentIds, each followed by a DLQ publish
Cross-check: audit, gateway, routing-execution, fraud-scoring, settlement show zero related errors/health-failures in the same window -- blast radius scoped to the two Mongo-reading services only
reasoning_trace:
Blind investigation (evidence read before checking injector's claimed root). Witness monitor showed validation-enrichment and aml-compliance both going DOWN within ~1.6s of each other (07:23:53.7 and 07:23:55.4) and RECOVERED together shortly after -- an immediate signal that whatever failed is shared between two otherwise-unrelated services, not a bug local to either.

Reading the raw ES events for those two services during the window confirmed the specific shared dependency: both emit repeated "MongoDB health check failed" / "Health contributor org.springframework.boot.actuate.data.mongo.MongoHealthIndicator (mongo) took ~30000ms to respond" messages, in near-lockstep, for the full ~60s duration. This alone could in principle be two independent MongoDB-adjacent bugs, so I looked for a second, structurally different evidence type: validation-enrichment's own driver layer directly reports "Timed out while waiting for a server that matches WritableServerSelector. Client view of cluster state is {type=UNKNOWN, ...}" on real in-flight payments (paymentId=e2d20740-..., 0d833851-..., etc.), each followed by a DLQ publish. That message is the MongoDB Java driver's own self-reported inability to reach a writable member of the replica set -- a direct, self-reported symptom naming MongoDB specifically, not an inference from correlated timing alone.

Ruled out: an app-level bug in either service individually (the correlated onset/recovery across two independently-deployed services rules this out -- a local bug wouldn't explain why both fail and recover at almost the same instant); a Redis or Cassandra dependency (no health-indicator or driver messages referencing either appear in the window); a network-wide outage (other services -- audit, gateway, routing-execution, fraud-scoring, settlement -- show zero health-check failures or errors in the same window, so the blast radius is scoped to exactly the two services that read Mongo-backed data, not the whole mesh).

Blind conclusion formed before reading the injector's claimed root: mongodb.
confirmation_basis: Blind conclusion (mongodb) matches injector_claimed_root exactly. Independent evidence: two unrelated services (validation-enrichment, aml-compliance) sharing an identical MongoDB health-indicator failure signature in near-lockstep, plus validation-enrichment self-reporting a MongoDB driver WritableServerSelector timeout directly naming the dependency -- not inferred solely from injector metadata.
